model.name: Application / Request Record
model.purpose: Govern the persistent record of an application or request that enters a case or service lifecycle, including identity, parties, requested service, evidence, state, and record controls, independently of storage format or access interface.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the instance-level application or request as captured evidence of a transaction: an identified request for a service, benefit, permit, procedure, or comparable action, submitted by or on behalf of a subject, received through a channel, assessed against requirements and evidence, and used to initiate or join a case or service execution. It is format-neutral and treats JSON, YAML, forms, messages, case-file items and database rows as projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Instance identity of an application or request, including master-system identifiers, governed IRIs, composite/requisition identifiers, and replacement lineage.
Classification of the request by type, category, intent, priority, and the service, procedure or activity being requested.
Parties and roles: subject/beneficiary, applicant, requester, representative, competent authority, intended performer, and other participants.
Triggering life or business event, submission channel, cost to the applicant, legal resources and operating rules that authorise the procedure.
Requirements, criteria, constraints, submitted evidence, evidence types, completeness, and once-only reuse or cross-border evidence exchange.
Composition with a case or case file, grouping of related requests, expected outputs, and dependencies on other services.
Request-intention status, record capture and registration, CaseFileItem lifecycle, withdrawal, amendment, hold, revocation, and processing-time commitments.
Event time versus observation/ingestion time, occurrence window, jurisdiction/spatial coverage, and place of performance.
Provenance, authenticity, integrity, reliability, usability, signatures, reported-versus-primary recording, confidentiality, access, audit, retention, archival and deletion.
out_of_scope: The catalogue definition of a public service that exists whether or not anyone applies (CPSV-AP Public Service as a portfolio/catalogue object).
The administrative case, docket or case-plan aggregate after initiation (sibling WM-POL-017 and CMMN Case).
Work-item or task execution tracking of fulfilment (FHIR Task and similar work-management objects).
Master records of persons, organisations, locations, assets or legal instruments except as references from the application.
Decision, determination, licence, permit, benefit award or other output artefacts except as expected or produced results linked from the request.
Blank form templates, user-interface widgets, storage formats, APIs, Git, MCP or database schemas as semantics.
Payment, fee-settlement and accounting transactions, except cost metadata attached to the service or channel.
Clinical procedure performance, observations and diagnostic reports that result from a healthcare ServiceRequest.
Freedom-of-information, subject-access and discovery requests as a distinct legal regime unless explicitly classified as this request type by the adopting Dimension.
IT incident, problem and change records that are not a request entering a service or case lifecycle.

boundary_notes.distinction: WM-REC-009 is a specialised record of an application or request transaction. Generic record characteristics (capture, classification, metadata, authenticity, retention) belong to the parent record model; this model adds request identity, intent, parties, service, evidence pack, and request-status semantics.

An administrative case may begin with an application or request, but the case is the continuing matter, plan and file. The application is typically an input or CaseFileItem that initiates or joins the case; case stages, sentries, milestones and fulfilment tasks are out of this model.

A Public Service exists whether used or not and describes inputs, channels, competent authority and processing time at catalogue level. This model records a particular agent's use of that service: the submitted instance, its evidence, status and capture as a record.

FHIR Request.status is the status of authorisation or intention, not execution. Fulfilment, acceptance by a performer, and in-progress work are tracked on Task or case plan items, not as the core semantics of the application record.

boundary_notes.neighbor: CCCEV Requirement and Evidence as standalone criteria objects
boundary_notes.distinction: Requirements, criteria and evidence types are reusable definitions held by a service. This model references those definitions and records the evidence actually provided with a specific application; it does not own the criterion catalogue.

Applicant, subject, requester, competent authority and spatial coverage are references to agent and location models. This model records participation, role and authority relative to the request, not civil-status or organisational master data.

sources.title: Core Public Service Vocabulary Application Profile (CPSV-AP) 3.2.0
sources.relevance: Defines Public Service, Event, Channel, Evidence, Requirement, Output, Cost, competent authority, processing time, legal resource and participation — the catalogue and interface context that an application instance uses.

sources.title: Core Criterion and Core Evidence Vocabulary (CCCEV) 2.1.0
sources.relevance: Defines Requirement, Criterion, Constraint, Evidence, Evidence Type, agents that create/issue/provide evidence, confidentiality, validity period and supported values used to assess an application.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR R5 Resource ServiceRequest
sources.relevance: Normative healthcare and general service-request instance: identifiers, requisition, status, intent, priority, code, subject, authoredOn, requester, performer, reason, supporting information, replacement and grouping.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR R5 Request pattern
sources.relevance: Cross-resource request pattern distinguishing proposal/plan/order, authorisation status versus fulfilment, occurrence, reported-versus-primary, insurance, deliver-to and do-not-perform.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Global records-management principles for creating, capturing and managing records in any format, including metadata, assigned responsibilities, business context and processes that make an application evidential.

sources.title: Case Management Model and Notation (CMMN) Version 1.1
sources.relevance: Defines Case, CaseFile, CaseFileItem, roles, case inputs/outputs and CaseFileItem lifecycle, the case-side composition of an application entering a case.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 Article 5 — Principles relating to processing of personal data
sources.relevance: Lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality and accountability for personal data typically present on applications.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 Article 14 — Technical system for the cross-border automated exchange of evidence and application of the once-only principle
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 of 2 October 2018; Article 14 (legislation.gov.uk record modified 2024-10-03)
sources.relevance: Once-only principle and cross-border automated evidence exchange for procedures accessed through the Single Digital Gateway, affecting how applications obtain evidence without re-collection.

sources.title: ISO 23081 Metadata for records
sources.relevance: Metadata framework for authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability of records, and for telling who did what to which digital object across the application record's life.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How an application or request instance is identified, typed, prioritised and bound to the service or activity being sought, distinct from catalogue identifiers and from later case identifiers.
bundles.rationale: FHIR and CPSV-AP both require identifiers; FHIR additionally separates requisition/group identifiers, replacement and intent. Without this bundle an agent cannot tell one filing from another or from the service definition it invokes.

layers.name: Instance identifiers
layers.description: Authoritative and secondary identifiers for the application instance, including composite requisitions and lineage of replacements.

findings.name: Application instance identity
findings.description: The application or request record must carry one or more business identifiers assigned by the receiving or originating system, optionally a governed IRI, and must not treat a date as an identifier. Composite filings share a requisition or group identifier; a later filing may replace an earlier one.

questions.text: Which master-system identifier is authoritative for this application instance, which system assigned it, and what is its identifier type?
Does a governed global IRI exist for this application distinct from the Public Service catalogue identifier and from any case identifier?
Is this filing part of a composite requisition or group of related requests, and if so what shared identifier binds them?
Which prior application or request does this filing replace, amend, or fulfil, and is the prior record revoked or superseded?

data_elements.name: Application identifier
data_elements.description: One or more business identifiers assigned to this order or application.

data_elements.name: Application IRI
data_elements.description: Optional governed IRI for the application instance, distinct from dct:identifier of the catalogue Public Service.

data_elements.name: Requisition or group identifier
data_elements.description: Composite request identifier shared by related filings.

data_elements.name: Replaces request
data_elements.description: Reference to the request this filing replaces.

data_elements.name: Based on
data_elements.description: Plan, proposal or prior request that this filing fulfils.

artifacts.name: Identity assignment or acknowledgement notice
artifacts.description: Instrument that communicates the authoritative application number or IRI to the applicant after capture.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the same authoritative application identifier as the record; if the notice is a separate serial, append a notice sequence under that identifier.

layers.name: Type, intent, priority and requested service
layers.description: What kind of request this is, with what authorisation intent and urgency, and what service or activity is being sought.

findings.name: Intent, category and priority
findings.description: A request is a specific intention bound to a subject and approximate timing. Intent (proposal, plan, directive, order) is immutable in the FHIR pattern. Category partitions the request for search, access control and behaviour. Priority distinguishes routine, urgent, asap and stat. A do-not-perform flag records a prohibition rather than a positive order.

questions.text: Is this filing a proposal, plan, directive, order, or another authorised intent, and is that intent immutable after capture?
Which categories partition this request for search, access control or routing, and from which controlled vocabulary?
What priority applies, who set it, and does it override default processing time for the channel or service?
Is the request a prohibition of an action rather than a request to perform one?

data_elements.name: Request intent
data_elements.description: proposal | plan | directive | order or locally extended intent; treated as immutable once active.

data_elements.name: Request category
data_elements.description: Classification used to filter, govern access or guide behaviour.

data_elements.name: Request priority
data_elements.description: routine | urgent | asap | stat or aligned local urgency code.

data_elements.name: Do not perform
data_elements.description: True if the request prohibits rather than authorises the action.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Intent, category, priority and prohibition are coded attributes of the request record itself; they are not independent serial artefacts unless a Dimension issues a separate priority-override instrument.

findings.name: Requested service or activity
findings.description: The application must name the Public Service, procedure or activity requested. CPSV-AP Public Service is the catalogue object; the application references it and may also carry a coded activity (FHIR ServiceRequest.code). Status of the catalogue service is not status of this filing.

questions.text: Which Public Service or procedure catalogue entry is this application invoking, and what is that service's identifier and name?
What coded activity, procedure or service is being requested or ordered beyond the catalogue reference?
Is the referenced Public Service currently offered (catalogue status), and is that distinct from this application's request status?

data_elements.name: Requested public service
data_elements.description: Reference to the CPSV-AP Public Service or equivalent catalogue procedure.

data_elements.name: Requested activity code
data_elements.description: Codeable reference for the service or procedure being requested.

data_elements.name: Order detail parameters
data_elements.description: Additional structured parameters for the requested service.

data_elements.name: Requested product
data_elements.description: Product requested or ordered where the request is for a product rather than a pure service.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The requested service is a reference plus optional coded parameters on the application record. The catalogue entry and any resulting licence or procedure report are sibling artefacts, not this finding's payload.

bundles.name: Parties, authority and channel
bundles.description: Who the request is for, who files it, who is competent to receive it, who should perform it, and through which channel it entered, including cost and availability constraints of that channel.
bundles.rationale: CPSV-AP binds every Public Service to a competent authority and channels; FHIR binds every request to a subject and optional requester and performer. Participation roles capture representatives and other agents.

layers.name: Actors and participation roles
layers.description: Subject, requester, reporter, representative and other participants, with role codes.

findings.name: Subject and applicant
findings.description: The subject is the individual, organisation, group, device or location the service is ordered or prohibited for. The applicant may be the same agent or a distinct filer. Evidence may be about a different agent than the filer.

questions.text: Who or what is the subject of the requested service, and which master identity is used?
Is the applicant the same agent as the subject, and if not what is the applicant's identity?
For each attached evidence, which agent is the evidence about, and does that match the application subject?

data_elements.name: Subject
data_elements.description: Agent, group, device or location the service is for or prohibited for.

data_elements.name: Applicant
data_elements.description: Agent who seeks the service; may equal subject.

data_elements.name: Evidence about agent
data_elements.description: Agent that is the subject of a piece of evidence.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject and applicant are references to agent masters; copies of identity documents are evidence artefacts under the evidence bundle, not this finding.

findings.name: Requester, representative and reporter
findings.description: Who/what is requesting the service may differ from the subject (practitioner, organisation, related person, device). A representative participation role and a reported-versus-primary flag record third-party or secondary capture.

questions.text: Who or what is requesting the service, and in what capacity relative to the subject?
Which participation roles are recorded (competent authority, service user, provider, representative) and who fills each?
Is this application a reported rather than primary record, and who reported it?

data_elements.name: Requester
data_elements.description: Who or what is requesting the service.

data_elements.name: Participation
data_elements.description: Role-bearing participation of an agent in the application or its public service.

data_elements.name: Reported rather than primary
data_elements.description: Indicates secondary or reported capture of the request.

data_elements.name: Reported by
data_elements.description: Agent who reported the request if not the primary recorder.

artifacts.name: Mandate or representation instrument
artifacts.description: Power of attorney, parental authority, professional mandate or similar instrument authorising a requester to file for a subject.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative instrument identifier from the issuing authority; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID linked to the application identifier.

layers.name: Competent authority, performer, channel and cost
layers.description: Who is ultimately responsible, who is desired to perform, how the application was lodged, and what it costs.

findings.name: Competent authority and intended performer
findings.description: CPSV-AP requires one or more competent authorities ultimately responsible for the Public Service, whether or not delivery is outsourced. FHIR separately records desired performer type and specific performer, and who should receive the result.

questions.text: Which Public Organization is the competent authority for the requested service, and is that the same body that will process this filing?
What kind of performer is desired and is a specific performer, care team or organisation named?
Who should receive the result of the request, and at which location or endpoint?

data_elements.name: Competent authority
data_elements.description: Public Organization ultimately responsible for the service.

data_elements.name: Desired performer type
data_elements.description: Coded kind of service performer sought.

data_elements.name: Specific desired performer
data_elements.description: Named performer, organisation, team or device.

data_elements.name: Deliver to
data_elements.description: Who should receive the result of the request.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Authority and performer are organisational references and role assignments; appointment letters or outsourcing contracts belong to organisation or contract siblings.

findings.name: Submission channel, availability and cost
findings.description: A Channel is the medium through which an agent interacts with the Public Service (online, phone, walk-in). Evidence required may vary by channel (for example digital versus wet signature). Cost may depend on channel. Opening hours and availability restrictions constrain lodging.

questions.text: Through which channel was this application lodged, who owns that channel, and what is its type?
Did the chosen channel impose different evidence or signature requirements than the service-level default?
What cost is payable by the citizen or business for this execution, and is it channel-dependent?
Was the channel within opening hours and free of availability restrictions at lodging time?

data_elements.name: Channel used
data_elements.description: Medium through which the application was lodged.

data_elements.name: Channel type
data_elements.description: Coded type such as online, phone or walk-in centre.

data_elements.name: Cost
data_elements.description: Cost related to execution of the public service for the applicant.

data_elements.name: Channel processing time
data_elements.description: Processing time associated with the chosen channel when it differs from the service default.

artifacts.name: Channel lodgement receipt
artifacts.description: Channel-generated proof of lodging (counter ticket, online submission receipt, call-reference).
artifacts.identity_strategy: Channel transaction identifier as issued by the channel owner; cross-link to the application authoritative identifier after registration.

bundles.name: Trigger, legal basis, requirements and evidence
bundles.description: Why the application is made, under which legal resources and rules, which requirements must be met, and which evidence is supplied, reused or still missing.
bundles.rationale: CPSV-AP links services to life/business events, legal resources, rules and required evidence. CCCEV models requirements, criteria, constraints and evidential proof, including confidentiality and validity. SDG Article 14 adds once-only reuse.

layers.name: Triggering event and legal framework
layers.description: Life or business events that hook the service, plus legal resources and rules the service follows.

findings.name: Triggering event and stated reason
findings.description: An Event (typically a Life Event or Business Event) relates a citizen or business situation to public services. FHIR independently records why the service is needed. The application should capture both the catalogue event hook and instance-level reasons.

questions.text: Which life or business event triggered this application, and what is that event's identifier and name?
Why is the service needed or prohibited for this subject, in coded and/or narrative form?
Does the instance reason align with the catalogue event that the Public Service is related to, or is this an atypical use?

data_elements.name: Triggering event
data_elements.description: Life Event or Business Event related to the Public Service.

data_elements.name: Event type
data_elements.description: Controlled vocabulary type of the event, for example the EU Business event NAL.

data_elements.name: Request reason
data_elements.description: Coded or referenced justification for why the service is (not) needed.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Events and reasons are references and codes on the application; underlying vital-event or business-registry proofs are evidence artefacts.

findings.name: Legal resource, rules and formal framework
findings.description: The Public Service may follow rules and have legal resources. CCCEV Reference Framework and CPSV-AP Rule/Legal Resource record the normative basis. Constraints are requirements that impose hard limits (age, turnover, residency).

questions.text: Which legal resources authorise or constrain this procedure, and at what identifier or ELI?
Which operational rules does this public service follow for accepting and processing the application?
Which hard constraints (minimum age, residency, thresholds) apply to this filing's information concepts?

data_elements.name: Legal resource
data_elements.description: Legislation or other legal resource linked to the public service.

data_elements.name: Rule
data_elements.description: Rule under which the public service operates.

data_elements.name: Constraint
data_elements.description: Limitation applied to an information concept, such as a minimum age.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Legal resources and rules are references to legislative and policy objects maintained outside this record; copies stored for evidential capture are handled as record artefacts under provenance.

layers.name: Requirements, evidence and completeness
layers.description: What must be proven, what was supplied, confidentiality and validity of evidence, and once-only reuse.

findings.name: Held requirements and criteria
findings.description: A Public Service holds requirements (residency, age, and similar). Criteria are requirements with an evaluation objective and optional weights. Information requirements request data that evidence must support. The application records which requirements apply and the assessment posture, not the criterion catalogue itself.

questions.text: Which requirements and criteria does this application have to satisfy, and which information concepts must be evidenced?
If criteria are weighted or biased for evaluation, what weights, weighting type and consideration description apply?
For each requirement, has evidence been provided, reused, waived, or is it still outstanding?

data_elements.name: Held requirement
data_elements.description: Requirement the public service holds and that this application must address.

data_elements.name: Criterion weight
data_elements.description: Relative importance of a criterion between 0 and 1.

data_elements.name: Requirement response state
data_elements.description: Whether the requirement is evidenced, outstanding, waived or failed.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Requirements and criteria are references to CCCEV/CPSV-AP definitions plus per-application response state; the definitional catalogue is a sibling.

findings.name: Submitted or reused evidence
findings.description: Evidence is proof that a requirement is met: it may verify a claim, prove a condition, or provide data, in any medium. Evidence records confidentiality, subject, conformance to an evidence type, creator, issuer, provider, supported requirement or value, and validity period. Service-level hasInput lists expected evidence; channel-level hasInput records channel-specific variants.

questions.text: What evidence objects are attached or linked, of which evidence types, and which requirements or information concepts do they support?
Who created, legally issued, and transmitted each evidence object, and what is its confidentiality classification?
During which period does each evidence hold true, and does it still satisfy the evidence type's validity-period constraint at assessment time?
answer_data: validity period start and end RFC 3339 or date

questions.text: What additional supporting information, specimens, notes or patient/applicant instructions accompany the request but are not formal evidence types?

data_elements.name: Evidence
data_elements.description: Proof that a requirement is met, in any structure, format or medium.

data_elements.name: Evidence type
data_elements.description: Desired form, content, source or other characteristics of evidence.

data_elements.name: Evidence confidentiality level
data_elements.description: Security classification assigned to an evidence object.

data_elements.name: Evidence validity period
data_elements.description: Period during which the evidence holds true or has force.

data_elements.name: Supporting information
data_elements.description: Additional information supporting the request.

data_elements.name: Insurance or coverage
data_elements.description: Coverage or claim-response references relevant to the request.

artifacts.name: Evidence item
artifacts.description: Document, registry extract, recording or other object offered as proof.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer's authoritative evidence identifier if present; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID, with hash for integrity.

findings.name: Completeness and once-only evidence exchange
findings.description: An application is complete relative to required evidence types. SDG Article 14 requires a technical system for cross-border automated exchange of evidence and application of the once-only principle so applicants need not re-supply evidence already held by administrations. Missing, waived, or exchanged evidence must be explicit.

questions.text: Relative to the applicable evidence type list, which required items are present, missing, waived, or substituted?
Was any evidence reused under the once-only principle rather than collected again from the applicant, and from which authority?
answer_data: legal basis SDG Article 14 or national equivalent

questions.text: Did this procedure use the cross-border automated evidence-exchange technical system, and what was the outcome?
Is the evidence collected limited to what is necessary for the specified purpose of this procedure?

data_elements.name: Completeness state
data_elements.description: Whether required evidence types are satisfied, partial, waived or incomplete.

data_elements.name: Once-only applied
data_elements.description: Whether evidence was reused rather than re-collected.

data_elements.name: Evidence exchange transaction
data_elements.description: Reference to a cross-border or domestic evidence-exchange transaction.

artifacts.name: Once-only evidence exchange record
artifacts.description: Record of a request and response for automated evidence reuse.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Exchange transaction identifier assigned by the once-only technical system; cross-link to application identifier.

bundles.name: Case composition and relationships
bundles.description: How the application enters a case or service execution, how it groups with other requests, what it is expected to produce, and which other services it requires first.
bundles.rationale: The registered relation WM-POL-017 COMPOSE states that an administrative case begins with an application. CMMN models Case inputs, CaseFile and CaseFileItems. CPSV-AP models produces/output and requires other services. FHIR models basedOn, replaces and group identifiers.

layers.name: Case file membership and request lineage
layers.description: Placement of the application in a case file and its relations to other requests.

findings.name: Case initiation and case file item
findings.description: A Case has a CaseFile of CaseFileItems and may declare inputs and outputs. An application is typically captured as a CaseFileItem and/or a Case input parameter that initiates or joins the case. CaseFileItem lifecycle is distinct from request-intention status.

questions.text: Does this application initiate a new case, join an existing case, or remain uncased, and what is the case identifier?
Which CaseFileItem represents this application in the case file, and what is its definition type and name?
answer_data: parent case file item if nested

questions.text: Which case roles are authorised in the resulting case, and how do they map from application participants?

data_elements.name: Related case
data_elements.description: Case initiated or joined by this application.

data_elements.name: Case file item
data_elements.description: CaseFileItem corresponding to this application or its attachments.

data_elements.name: Case input
data_elements.description: Case input parameter bound to this application.

artifacts.name: Application as case file item
artifacts.description: The application instrument as filed in the case dossier.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Case file item identifier assigned by the case system, cross-walked to the application authoritative identifier.

findings.name: Expected outputs, service dependencies and request lineage
findings.description: Public services produce outputs and may require prior services. Requests may be based on plans or prior requests and may be grouped. Encounter or episode context may bind a healthcare request.

questions.text: What output is this application expected to produce (permit, decision, report, physical object), and is that output already referenced?
Must other public services be executed first, and have their outputs been supplied as evidence?
answer_data: linked prior application or output identifiers

questions.text: Is this request tied to an encounter, episode, care plan or other operational context?

data_elements.name: Expected output
data_elements.description: Output the public service is expected to produce.

data_elements.name: Requires public service
data_elements.description: Other public service whose output is needed before execution.

data_elements.name: Encounter
data_elements.description: Encounter the request is tied to, where applicable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Outputs and prerequisite services are references; the actual decision, licence or diagnostic report is a sibling artefact produced later in the case.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, time and place
bundles.description: Request-intention status, record capture, case-file-item states, withdrawals and holds, event versus observation time, processing-time commitments, jurisdiction and location of performance.
bundles.rationale: FHIR isolates authorisation status from fulfilment. ISO 15489 requires capture as a record. CMMN defines CaseFileItem lifecycle including Available and Discarded. CPSV-AP supplies processing time and spatial coverage. FHIR occurrence and authoredOn separate when the service should happen from when the request was created.

layers.name: Status, capture and exception paths
layers.description: Authorisation lifecycle, records capture, and rare paths such as withdrawal, hold, amendment and discard.

findings.name: Request intention status
findings.description: Request status is draft, active, on-hold, revoked, completed, entered-in-error or unknown, optionally with a status reason. This is the status of authorisation or intention, not of work execution. Completed means the authorisation is fulfilled as an intention, which must not be confused with case closure.

questions.text: What is the current request-intention status and the reason for that status?
Is fulfilment being tracked separately from this status, and if so on which task or case plan items?
Was the application entered in error, and what corrective action replaced or nullified it?

data_elements.name: Request status
data_elements.description: draft | active | on-hold | revoked | completed | entered-in-error | unknown.

data_elements.name: Status reason
data_elements.description: Reason for the current status.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Intention status is a coded attribute of the request; status-change notices may exist as serial correspondence but are not required by the cited request pattern.

findings.name: Record capture and case file item lifecycle
findings.description: ISO 15489 applies to creation, capture and management of records regardless of structure or form. Capture makes the application evidential. CMMN CaseFileItem lifecycle includes transitions such as Available to Discarded and child add/remove. These states are sibling to request-intention status.

questions.text: Has this application been captured as a record, by which records system, and under which classification or file code?
What is the CaseFileItem lifecycle state of this application in the case file (for example available or discarded)?
Which roles are assigned responsibility for creating, capturing, monitoring and disposing of this application record?

data_elements.name: Captured as record
data_elements.description: Whether the application has been captured into a records system.

data_elements.name: Records classification
data_elements.description: Business classification or file code assigned at capture.

data_elements.name: Case file item state
data_elements.description: Lifecycle state of the corresponding CaseFileItem.

artifacts.name: Capture and registration entry
artifacts.description: Records-system registration of the application as a captured record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Records-system registration identifier as master; cross-walk to application identifier.

findings.name: Withdrawal, amendment, hold and revocation
findings.description: Applicants may withdraw; authorities may revoke or place on hold; later filings may replace. CMMN discard removes a CaseFileItem. These are first-class exception paths, not mere status comments.

questions.text: Has the applicant withdrawn the application, when, and does the record remain captured for evidence of the transaction?
Is the request on hold or revoked, by whom, and what status reason applies?
If the application was amended, is the amendment a patch to the same record or a replacing request with lineage?

data_elements.name: Withdrawal time
data_elements.description: When the applicant withdrew the application.

data_elements.name: Hold or revoke actor
data_elements.description: Agent who placed the request on hold or revoked it.

data_elements.name: Amendment mode
data_elements.description: Whether change is an in-place patch or a replacing request.

artifacts.name: Withdrawal, hold, revocation or amendment notice
artifacts.description: Applicant or authority instrument that changes the request path.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative notice identifier from the issuing party; link to application identifier and, if replacing, to the new request identifier.

layers.name: Temporal and spatial context
layers.description: When the request was authored, when the service should occur, how long processing should take, where jurisdiction and performance lie.

findings.name: Event time, authored time and processing time
findings.description: AuthoredOn is when the request was created or transitioned to active. Occurrence is when the service should (not) occur. Processing time is a duration commitment on the service or channel. Event time and observation/ingestion time must be recorded separately when they differ. All timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. A date is not an identifier.

questions.text: When was this request created or transitioned to active, in RFC 3339 with an explicit offset or Z?
When should the requested service occur or not occur — as an instant, period or timing schedule?
What processing-time duration does the service or channel commit to, and has it been exceeded relative to authored or capture time?
If observation or ingestion time differs from the applicant's event time of lodging, what are both values?

data_elements.name: Authored on
data_elements.description: When the request was created or became active.

data_elements.name: Occurrence
data_elements.description: When the service should or should not occur.

data_elements.name: Processing time
data_elements.description: Declared duration for executing the public service or channel.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: Applicant-side time of lodging or of the triggering event.

data_elements.name: Ingestion or observation time
data_elements.description: When the receiving system observed or ingested the application.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Times and durations are typed values on the record. SLA breach notices, if issued, are correspondence artefacts under process exceptions rather than this finding.

findings.name: Jurisdiction, spatial coverage and place of performance
findings.description: Public Organization and Public Service have spatial coverage (administrative regions). Requests may name a location of performance. Channel walk-in centres are locations. Geometry is optional via Core Location.

questions.text: Which administrative region or jurisdiction does the requested service and competent authority cover, and is the subject in-scope?
Where should the service be performed, if location-specific?
If lodged in person, at which office or address was the application received?

data_elements.name: Spatial coverage
data_elements.description: Administrative region covered by the service or competent authority.

data_elements.name: Performance location
data_elements.description: Location where the service should be performed.

data_elements.name: Lodgement location
data_elements.description: Place of in-person or posted lodgement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Spatial values are references to location or region authorities; maps and geometries belong to the location sibling model.

bundles.name: Provenance, quality, privacy, access and retention
bundles.description: Who did what to the application record, whether it is authentic and usable, how personal data are minimised and classified, who may access it, and how long it is kept or destroyed.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 and ISO 23081 require metadata that supports authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability. GDPR Article 5 constrains personal data on applications. Evidence confidentiality and records disposal complete the operating surface.

layers.name: Provenance, authenticity and quality
layers.description: Capture metadata, integrity, signatures and quality of the application as a record.

findings.name: Provenance, authenticity, integrity and usability
findings.description: Records metadata must tell who did what to which digital object so authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability can be asserted over time, independent of format. Evidence additionally distinguishes creator, legal issuer and transmitter.

questions.text: Who captured, classified, classified-security, modified or transmitted this application record, using which system, and when?
What integrity measure (hash, signature, seal) protects the application payload and each evidence item?
On what basis is the application asserted authentic and reliable (original capture, qualified signature, registry-sourced evidence)?
Can the record still be interpreted in the business context of the people and processes that created it, including language and rendering?

data_elements.name: Provenance event
data_elements.description: Agent-action-object-time tuple for a significant records event.

data_elements.name: Integrity hash
data_elements.description: Fixity information for the application payload.

data_elements.name: Language
data_elements.description: Language of the application content.

data_elements.name: Signature or seal quality
data_elements.description: Level or type of electronic or wet signature applied.

artifacts.name: Signed application instrument
artifacts.description: The signed or sealed application as captured, including any qualified electronic signature container.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative application identifier plus signature-container identifier if the signature is a detached object.

layers.name: Privacy, access, retention and deletion
layers.description: Personal-data principles, confidentiality, access, audit, storage limitation and archival exception.

findings.name: Personal data principles and confidentiality
findings.description: Application records typically contain personal data that must be processed lawfully, for specified purposes, minimised, accurate, storage-limited, and secured. Evidence may carry an explicit confidentiality level. The controller must demonstrate compliance.

questions.text: What is the specified, explicit and legitimate purpose and lawful basis for processing personal data on this application?
Which personal data elements are necessary for this procedure, and which were collected in excess or not collected under minimisation?
Are personal data accurate and up to date, and what rectification or erasure steps have been taken without delay?
What confidentiality or security classification applies to the application and to each evidence item?

data_elements.name: Processing purpose
data_elements.description: Specified purpose for processing personal data on the application.

data_elements.name: Lawful basis
data_elements.description: Lawful basis for processing.

data_elements.name: Controller
data_elements.description: Controller responsible for demonstrating compliance.

data_elements.name: Application confidentiality
data_elements.description: Security classification of the application record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Purpose, lawful basis and classification are metadata of the record. Data-protection impact assessments and records of processing are organisation-level artefacts, not instance serials of this finding.

findings.name: Access control and audit
findings.description: Access is governed by role, classification and purpose. Integrity and confidentiality require protection against unauthorised processing. Audit must show who accessed or changed the application.

questions.text: Who may read this application at bundle, layer, finding and artefact scope, and under what purpose limitation?
What access exceptions exist (legal privilege, whistleblower, sealed minor, law-enforcement overlay)?
What audit events must be retained to demonstrate who accessed or altered the application and its evidence?

data_elements.name: Access policy
data_elements.description: Policy governing read and change of the application.

data_elements.name: Access exception
data_elements.description: Recorded exception to the default access rule.

artifacts.name: Access and change audit log
artifacts.description: Chronology of access and mutation events for the application record and attached evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Audit sequence under the application authoritative identifier plus event timestamp RFC 3339.

findings.name: Retention, archival and deletion
findings.description: Personal data must not identify data subjects longer than necessary, with an archival/research exception under appropriate safeguards. ISO 15489 requires disposal as a controlled records process, which may retain evidential copies beyond operational need. These two clocks can conflict and must both be recorded.

questions.text: What records retention schedule and disposal action apply to this application and its evidence?
When does the GDPR storage-limitation clock expire for identifiable personal data, and is further processing solely archival, research or statistical?
Has the record been deleted, anonymised, or transferred to an archive, and what evidential residue remains?

data_elements.name: Retention schedule
data_elements.description: Records schedule governing this application class.

data_elements.name: Disposal action
data_elements.description: Destroy, transfer to archive, or review.

data_elements.name: Storage limitation end
data_elements.description: When identifiable personal data should no longer be kept for the original purpose.

data_elements.name: Archival exception
data_elements.description: Whether further processing is solely archival, scientific, historical or statistical.

artifacts.name: Disposal or transfer record
artifacts.description: Authorised destruction, anonymisation or archival transfer of the application record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Disposal-authority identifier from the records authority; retain even after the application payload is destroyed.

functions.name: Capture application as a record
functions.description: Receive a lodging through a channel, assign identity, record authored and ingestion times, and capture the application as evidential record metadata.
preconditions: channel is an accepted medium for the Public Service
subject identity is resolvable or explicitly anonymous per policy
effects: application exists as a captured record independent of original format
ingestion time is recorded if it differs from event time

functions.name: Validate requirements and evidence completeness
functions.description: Evaluate the filing against held requirements, evidence types, channel-specific inputs, constraints and data-minimisation rules.
preconditions: requested public service or activity is identified
effects: application is marked complete, partial, waived or incomplete
excess personal data may be flagged for suppression

functions.name: Register and acknowledge
functions.description: Make the request active as an intention, notify the applicant of the authoritative identifier, and optionally initiate a case.
outputs: optional case and case file item
preconditions: minimum mandatory elements present unless policy allows incomplete lodging
effects: applicant can cite the authoritative identifier

functions.name: Reuse or exchange evidence (once-only)
functions.description: Request evidence from another authority instead of re-collecting it from the applicant, including cross-border automated exchange where applicable.
preconditions: once-only or equivalent legal basis applies
technical system available or national reuse path exists
effects: evidence is linked without a second collection from the applicant

functions.name: Amend or replace request
functions.description: Apply an in-place amendment or create a replacing request that revokes or supersedes the prior filing while preserving lineage.
outputs: patched record or new application with replaces relation
preconditions: current status allows amendment or replacement
actor is applicant, representative or competent authority

functions.name: Withdraw, hold or revoke
functions.description: Applicant withdrawal or authority hold/revocation of the intention, without implying that the record is uncaptured.
outputs: updated request status and status reason
preconditions: request is not already entered-in-error or discarded contrary to policy
effects: record remains for evidence unless disposal policy says otherwise

functions.name: Link application to case file
functions.description: Create or join a case, add the application as a CaseFileItem and bind case inputs and roles.
preconditions: case model exists for the procedure
effects: application is inspectable as a dossier item
case roles are populated from participants

functions.name: Transition intention status
functions.description: Move request status among draft, active, on-hold, revoked, completed, entered-in-error or unknown with a recorded reason, without encoding fulfilment work.
preconditions: transition is legal from current status
effects: fulfilment tasks if any are not implicitly completed

functions.name: Dispose or transfer the application record
functions.description: Apply the records schedule and personal-data storage limitation: destroy, anonymise, or transfer to archive with residual disposal evidence.
preconditions: retention trigger fired or storage limitation reached
effects: payload may be destroyed while disposal certificate remains
archival exception documented if identity is retained

composition.purpose: Specialise the general record with application/request identity, intention status, parties, service, evidence pack and channel semantics while inheriting capture, classification, authenticity and retention.
An administrative case begins with an application or request; the application is an input or CaseFileItem of the case, not the case itself.

Align requested procedure, competent authority, channel, cost, processing time, legal resource, required evidence types and expected outputs with the public-service catalogue without absorbing catalogue semantics.
Reference reusable requirements, criteria, constraints and evidence types; store instance evidence and response state on the application.

Align instance identifiers, intent, status, priority, subject, requester, occurrence, authoredOn, replacement, grouping and do-not-perform with the FHIR request pattern without claiming healthcare-only scope.
Place the captured application and its evidence in a case file with a distinct item lifecycle (including available and discarded).
Point to subject, applicant, requester, competent authority, issuer and evidence subjects without duplicating civil or organisational master data.
Align evidence reuse and cross-border automated exchange with the Single Digital Gateway once-only principle where that regime applies.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the adopting Dimension's records authority as owner or maintainer of application-record policy, classification and disposal.
Bind each deployed package to the Public Service or procedure catalogue it may invoke, including competent authorities and channels.
Publish identifier namespaces, evidence-type lists and status vocabularies used by the Dimension, with mapping to CPSV-AP, CCCEV and FHIR where claimed.
Require AGENTS.md at the package root even when the store is MongoDB, a filesystem, or an MCP interface.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-owned IRI stem for application instances, distinct from CPSV-AP public-service IRIs and from case IRIs. Prefer the receiving authority's application number as the master identifier; mint a UUID or ULID only when no master-system identifier exists. Do not use dates as identifiers.
registry_links: Alignments: CPSV-AP Public Service, CCCEV Evidence, FHIR ServiceRequest, CMMN CaseFileItem

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity order is: authoritative master-system identifier; governed global IRI; Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.
Canonical timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; event time and ingestion time are separate fields when they differ.
Status vocabularies must distinguish request-intention status from case/fulfilment state and from CaseFileItem state.
Evidence objects are referenced, not inlined as opaque blobs, except for small structured supported values.
Language-tagged names and descriptions follow the multiplicity used by CPSV-AP (skos:prefLabel / dct:title patterns).
patch_rules: Intent is treated as immutable after the request leaves draft, matching the FHIR request pattern; changing intent requires a replacing request.

In-place patches may update notes, supporting information, completeness state and non-identity metadata; identity, subject and requested service changes SHOULD create a replacing request with replaces lineage.
Withdrawal, hold and revocation are status transitions with notices, not silent deletes.
Evidence add/remove follows CaseFileItem child add/remove semantics when the application sits in a case file.
compatibility_rules: Do not claim CPSV-AP, FHIR, CMMN or ISO 15489 conformance without a recorded mapping and validation evidence.
Where FHIR Request.status and a local administrative status list diverge, store both and declare which is canonical for the Dimension.
Catalogue Public Service status must not be overwritten by instance request status.
Once-only exchange identifiers remain in their issuing technical system's namespace.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the receiving or originating application register.
Governed global identifier or IRI under the Dimension or authority namespace.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event and observation timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record event time and observation/ingestion time separately when they differ; a date is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts are named by artefact type, authoritative application identifier, and a monotonic serial or RFC 3339 event time, for example application-notice-{application-id}-{nnn}.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artefact SHALL record fixity (hash) and, where a signature or seal is required by channel or evidence type, a verifiable signature container; ISO 23081-style provenance must say who did what to which object.

policies: Applications containing personal data are processed under specified purposes, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, and integrity/confidentiality, with the controller able to demonstrate compliance.
Capture as a record is mandatory once the lodging is accepted for business use; draft proposals may exist pre-capture under explicit policy.
Once-only reuse SHALL be preferred over re-collection where a legal and technical path exists, with exchange provenance retained.
Disposal follows the records schedule and does not silently defeat evidential retention or GDPR archival safeguards.

read: Default deny except to the applicant/subject (or mandated representative), assigned competent-authority processors, and records authority, scoped by classification.
Evidence with higher confidentiality than the application envelope requires a separate authorisation.
Audit reads of who accessed the record are themselves role-restricted.
create: Create is allowed through declared channels of the Public Service by the applicant, a mandated representative, or an authorised intake officer.
Automated once-only evidence attach is allowed to the creating process under the exchange legal basis.
Bulk or bot creation requires a Dimension policy; it is not implied by this model.
update: Applicant-initiated updates after active status are amendments or replacing requests, not silent rewrites.
Competent authority may update status, completeness, classification and case linkage.
Integrity hashes are recomputed on any payload change and prior bytes remain in provenance.
delete: Operational delete is not allowed; use entered-in-error, withdraw/revoke, or records disposal.
GDPR erasure is a disposal action with residual certificate, not an unlogged physical delete.
CaseFileItem discard does not by itself destroy the records copy unless the schedule says so.

roles.name: Applicant or subject
responsibilities: Lodge, amend or withdraw the application through an accepted channel.
Supply or consent to reuse of evidence.

roles.name: Representative or requester
responsibilities: File on behalf of the subject under a recorded mandate.
Ensure the mandate instrument is captured as evidence.

roles.name: Competent authority processor
responsibilities: Accept or refuse lodgement, validate completeness, set intention status, and link to a case.
Apply channel, cost and processing-time rules.

roles.name: Records authority
responsibilities: Own classification, capture rules, authenticity metadata and disposal.
Authorise transfer or destruction and retain disposal certificates.

roles.name: Evidence issuer or providing authority
responsibilities: Issue or transmit evidence, including once-only exchange responses.
State validity period and confidentiality of evidence.

roles.name: Controller (personal data)
responsibilities: Determine purpose and lawful basis, demonstrate Article 5 compliance, and handle rectification and erasure.

access.default_rule: Default deny. Read and change are granted by role, purpose, and confidentiality classification at each scope; the applicant or mandated representative may read their own non-sealed filing.
exceptions: Sealed filings (minors, protected identities, whistleblowing) hide subject identity from general processors.
Law-enforcement or court overlays may freeze disposal and widen or narrow access under a recorded legal basis.
Once-only providing authorities see evidence-request metadata, not necessarily the full application.
audit_requirements: Log create, read of classified evidence, status change, amendment, evidence add/remove, case link, exchange, and disposal with agent, action, object and RFC 3339 time.
Retain audit logs at least as long as the application record or as required by the controller's accountability policy, whichever is longer.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Then read the specification document at Specification URL for canonical semantics of WM-REC-009.
Then use Interface URL and Processes URL; treat Storage type URL as a projection, not as meaning.

coverage.claim: Wide-union, format-neutral context structure for an application or request record that enters a case or service lifecycle, grounded in CPSV-AP, CCCEV, FHIR Request/ServiceRequest, ISO 15489/23081, CMMN, GDPR Article 5 and SDG Article 14, with explicit non-conformance and regional limits.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifiers, IRI, requisition/group id, replaces/basedOn, identity priority rule.
Request-intention status, ISO capture, CMMN CaseFileItem states, withdraw/hold/revoke/amend, disposal.
Subject, requester, competent authority, performer, case, prior services, evidence about-agents, deliver-to.
authoredOn, occurrence, processing time, event versus ingestion time, evidence validity periods, RFC 3339 rule.
ISO 23081 who-did-what, evidence creator/issuer/provider, reported-versus-primary, signatures and hashes.
Records authority, competent authority, controller, channel owner, Dimension package owner.
Requirements, constraints, evidence types, completeness state, catalogue-versus-instance status checks.
Default deny, role scopes at bundle/layer/finding/artefact, sealed-file exceptions, audit log.
Records schedule versus GDPR storage limitation and archival exception; disposal certificates; no silent delete.
Alignments to CPSV-AP, CCCEV, FHIR, CMMN, SDG once-only exchange; conflicts recorded rather than claimed as conformance.
Intent, category, priority, activity code, event type, COFOG/sector left on the service catalogue.
CCCEV evidence object, types, confidentiality, validity, supportingInfo, once-only reuse.
GDPR Article 5 principles applied to application personal data.
Service/authority spatial coverage, performance location, lodgement place.
Competent authority, legal resources, rules, mandates, signature quality.
No primary source treats robotic actuation as part of an application/request record; factor_robotics in the registry is 0.

known_omissions: Full ISO 15489-1:2016 and ISO 23081-1:2017 clause text was not retrieved (ISO OBP served unrelated documents); capture/authenticity/disposal semantics rely on ISO/TC 46/SC 11 first-party summaries.
CMMN CaseFileItem lifecycle states beyond Available and Discarded (clause 8.3) were not fully enumerated from the PDF extract; remaining states are a gap.

National administrative-procedure acts (US APA, member-state APAs), MoReq2010, ICA Records in Contexts, NIEM petition/application exchanges, and ITIL service-request definitions were not fetched and are not claimed.
SDG Article 14 body text was only partially recovered (title and once-only framing); implementing regulation (EU) 2022/1463 OOTS details are omitted.
Legal capacity of minors, deceased applicants, anonymous/whistleblower lodgements, quota/lottery allocation, and FOI/SAR as request types lack primary support here.
Qualified electronic signature profiles (eIDAS) are implied by channel evidence variance but not modelled from an eIDAS primary text.
Fee payment and refund as a condition of admissibility is only present as CPSV-AP Cost, not as a financial transaction model.
conflicts: FHIR Request.status is authorisation/intention, not fulfilment; many administrative systems encode received/under-review/decided on the application itself — both views must be stored if used, with canonical declared.
CPSV-AP Public Service exists whether used or not; conflating catalogue status with application status is a modelling error.
GDPR storage limitation versus ISO 15489 evidential retention: archival/research exception exists but is not automatic; Dimensions must record which clock wins.
Channel-level hasInput versus service-level hasInput can disagree; CPSV-AP says use channel level only when evidence truly varies.
CMMN CaseFileItem discard does not equal records destruction or FHIR entered-in-error.
This model aligns to the cited standards; it does not claim conformance to any of them.
regional_assumptions: CPSV-AP, CCCEV, SDG and GDPR are European Union instruments; competent-authority language cites the Services Directive 2006/123/EC as reused by CPSV-AP.
FHIR ServiceRequest examples are healthcare-centric; the Request pattern is used here as a cross-domain analogue, which HL7 presents as informative, not a universal civic-application schema.
ISO 15489 and CMMN are treated as globally applicable records and case frames.
Once-only cross-border exchange applies to SDG in-scope procedures among participating states; other jurisdictions need a local reuse policy.
Administrative-region spatial values in Europe are expected to use ATU or equivalent named-authority lists per CPSV-AP guidance.
adversarial_checks: A freedom-of-information or subject-access request is a different legal regime; including it requires an explicit Dimension classification, not silent reuse of this model.
A licence, permit or benefit decision is an output, not the application; treating the award instrument as WM-REC-009 would duplicate the decision sibling.
doNotPerform / negative requests and mandatory notifications (no discretionary ask) are in the FHIR pattern but under-specified for civic notice-filings — marked as edge, not dropped.
Verbal or phone lodgements are in-scope as channel types; absence of a signed form does not mean absence of a record if ISO 15489 capture occurs.
Death or loss of capacity of the applicant mid-process is not specified in the cited primary sources and must not be invented as a canonical state.
Automated or robotic filing is not supported by primary sources retrieved; bot intake is a policy exception, not a core class.
